issues.title: Component-member navigation: follow-ups from #335
issues.body:
Follow-up work from the review of #335 (which implements #296). None of this blocks that PR — the two panics raised there are the only blocking items. This issue collects everything else, roughly in priority order.

## 1. Member navigation inside anonymous Blade components

Today a `wire:` value, `$this->member`, or bare `$var` inside a non-Livewire partial resolves to nothing, silently.

Take `resources/views/components/save-button.blade.php` containing `wire:click="save"`, used as `<x-save-button />` inside a Livewire component's view:

```
view_name_for_path(.../components/save-button.blade.php)  ->  "components.save-button"
render_source_files("components.save-button")             ->  []      (nobody calls view('components.save-button'))
livewire_name_for_path(...)                               ->  None    (not under livewire's view_path)
detect_inline_livewire_class(partial content)             ->  false   (no front matter)
                                                          =>  blade_backing_class_sources = []
```

`blade_backing_class_files` resolves the backing class from the file's **own** view name, but a partial's backing class is a property of whoever rendered it. Finding it requires walking **up** the usage graph to the enclosing Livewire component.

**Decision: traverse up and return the first match, not all matches.** At runtime a partial has exactly one `$this` — the component that rendered it — so a single target models Livewire's actual behaviour. A multi-result picker would be technically honest about static ambiguity but wrong about how the code runs.

**"First match" only means something if the order is deterministic.** `render_source_files` currently iterates a `HashMap` without sorting (see item 6), so any first-match traversal must sort or it will flap between parents.

What exists to build on:

- `salsa_impl.rs:10398` `handle_find_view_references` is already a Salsa-backed reverse "who references view X" lookup — but it only matches `@extends` and `@include`, not `<x-...>` tags or `<livewire:...>`, which is how anonymous components are actually used.
- `ParsedPatternsData` already carries `components` and `livewire_refs` per file (`salsa_impl.rs:5607`), Salsa-cached. A reverse component-usage index is a query over data that is already computed, not a new parse.

Needs a transitive walk (partials nest) with a cycle guard, and should be built on Salsa rather than the current uncached path — see item 7.

## 2. Hover card shows `Component::` for inline SFC and Volt classes

`this_member_hover_card` derives its header from `php_class::extract_class_fqn`, whose regex requires `class` at the start of a line. An anonymous `new class extends Component {` never matches, so the card falls back to the literal string `"Component"` and renders `Component::increment()` instead of naming the component.

Navigation itself is unaffected and correct — this is the card's label only.

Two further wrinkles in the same function: `extract_class_fqn` reads from **disk** while `blade_backing_class_sources` uses the **live editor buffer**, so the two disagree on unsaved edits; and the existing test only asserts `card.contains("::increment()")`, so it cannot detect this.

Suggested fix: for inline classes, fall back to the resolved Livewire component name (via `livewire_name_for_path`) rather than a hardcoded `"Component"`.

## 3. Functional Volt components resolve nothing

`blade_backing_class_sources` gates inline-class support on `detect_inline_livewire_class`, whose regex requires `new class extends ...Component`. A functional Volt file has no class at all:

```php
<?php
use function Livewire\Volt\{state};
state(['count' => 0]);
$increment = fn () => $this->count++;
?>
<div wire:click="increment">
```

So `wire:click="increment"` gets nothing, and neither does `$count`. The targets exist and are in the same file — `state([...])` keys are the properties, top-level `$name = fn () => ...` assignments are the actions.

Most of the machinery is already here: `livewire_resolver.rs:531` `VOLT_FUNCTIONAL_CALLS` already detects these files, and `view_var_index.rs:614` already parses `state(['user' => User::first()])` for variable typing. This is wiring, not new parsing.

(The #296 acceptance criteria named only class-based Volt, so this was correctly out of scope for #335.)

## 4. `wire:target` should navigate

`wire_value_kind` classifies `target` as a non-member attribute, but `wire:target` names an action method. Move it to `WireValueKind::Method`.

Two details worth handling at the same time:

- `wire:target="save, delete"` is legal Livewire. `is_php_identifier` rejects the whole string, so it will silently not navigate. Split on `,` and use the segment under the cursor.
- `wire:target` can also name a property when paired with `wire:model` loading states. This costs nothing today because goto ignores the Method/Property distinction entirely (item 5), but it becomes wrong once that distinction is enforced.

## 5. Goto discards the Method/Property distinction

`wire_attribute_target_at` carefully returns `WireTarget::Method` vs `WireTarget::Property`, then `wire_attribute_goto_definition` unwraps both to a bare `&str` and hands it to `locate_member`, which matches either kind. So `wire:model="save"` navigates to the method `save()`, where the AC says a data binding resolves to a property. Thread the expected kind through and filter on it.

## 6. `locate_member` traversal order, and cross-declaration leakage

`component_member_locator::locate_member` walks the tree with `stack.pop()`, which visits children in **reverse** order. Its doc comment says "in document order; returns the first match" — that is not what it does:

```php
class A { public $dup = 1; }   // line 2
class B { public $dup = 2; }   // line 5
// locate_member returns line 5
```

Related: `public_property_types` and `public_action_method_names` collect from **every** class, trait, and enum in the file. A trait declared alongside the component leaks its members into completion — which quietly contradicts the "trait-provided members are a known limitation" carve-out documented in #335.

Also in this bucket: `render_source_files` (`view_var_index.rs:145`) iterates a `HashMap` without sorting, while `vars_for_view` directly below it sorts for exactly this reason. Any "first match wins" consumer of it is nondeterministic.

## 7. Backing-class resolution bypasses Salsa and scans the whole index per keystroke

`render_source_files` is an O(entire index) linear scan. It is reached via `blade_backing_class_files` -> `blade_backing_class_sources`, which runs on **every keystroke inside a `wire:` value**, on every `$` completion, and on every `$this->member` hover and goto. Each hit is then followed by a blocking `std::fs::read_to_string` and a full tree-sitter PHP parse, uncached.

On a large app that is a linear sweep over every file with a `view(...)` call, per character typed. `CLAUDE.md` is explicit that all file parsing goes through Salsa inputs; this path does not. Item 1's graph walk should not be built on top of it until this is addressed.

## 8. `@props` default values are captured as local bindings

`is_template_local_binding` -> `collect_quoted_names` grabs every quoted token on an `@props`/`@aware` line, values included. `@props(['color' => 'blue'])` therefore marks `$blue` as locally bound and suppresses its navigation, as does any unrelated quoted text elsewhere on that line.

Low blast radius — `@props` files rarely have a backing class — but it is a false positive in the shadowing logic. Parse the array keys rather than scanning for quoted runs.

  - [ ] `$name = computed(fn() => ...)` and `$name = action(fn() => ...)` wrapped forms (also detected by `VOLT_FUNCTIONAL_CALLS`) resolve the same way, with a regression test for at least one wrapped form.
  - [ ] The hover card for a functional-Volt member also names the component via `livewire_name_for_path` (never falls back to `"Component"`, since `extract_class_fqn` finds no class in a functional file) — with a test.
- [ ] **Item 4 — `wire:target` navigates.** `wire_value_kind` classifies `target` so `wire:target="save, delete"` navigates to whichever of `save`/`delete` the cursor is on (split on `,`, resolve the segment under the cursor).
  - [ ] `wire:target` naming a property used with `wire:model`'s loading state (not an action) still resolves via goto — not silently broken by Item 5's Method/Property filter — with a regression test covering both the action form and the loading-state property form.
- [ ] **Item 5 — every kind-aware consumer of `locate_member` respects the Method vs. Property distinction**, not goto alone: `wire_attribute_goto_definition`, the hover-card path, and completion all thread `WireTarget::Method`/`WireTarget::Property` through and filter on it. `wire:model="save"` no longer navigates to, or shows a hover card for, the method `save()`. Regression tests cover goto and the hover-card path separately.
- [ ] **Item 6 — `locate_member` returns true document-order first match; completion excludes all non-owning declarations.**
  - [ ] All candidate declarations are collected via full traversal (no early return) and sorted by `(line, column)` before picking the first — not a queue-based BFS reorder — with a test nesting one candidate inside a trait body that appears before a shallow class, to catch BFS-vs-true-document-order divergence.
  - [ ] `public_property_types`/`public_action_method_names` scope to the single class/trait that is the actual component's declaration, excluding members from every other top-level class, trait, and enum in the file — with a test using two unrelated top-level classes (not just a trait) sharing a member name.
  - [ ] `render_source_files` (`view_var_index.rs:145`) sorts its output the same way `vars_for_view` already does, so first-match consumers are deterministic.
- [ ] **Item 7 — backing-class resolution is Salsa-cached, not a per-keystroke linear scan.**
  - [ ] `render_source_files`, `blade_backing_class_files`, and `blade_backing_class_sources` are converted to `#[salsa::tracked]` queries.
  - [ ] The query is tracked against the backing PHP class file's content, not just the blade file's: a regression test edits the backing class file and confirms the cached result invalidates and updates on the next call, rather than serving stale.
  - [ ] A regression test invokes the same goto/hover path twice with unchanged input and asserts, via call-count instrumentation or Salsa's query-invocation tracking, that the underlying file-read/parse scan executes once, not twice.
  - [ ] Item 1's transitive walk is verified to call the new Salsa-backed accessor, not the old uncached scan (e.g. by removing the old path so nothing else can call it, or an explicit call-count assertion).
- [ ] **Item 8 — `@props`/`@aware` default values are not captured as local bindings.** `@props(['color' => 'blue'])` binds only the key `color`, not the value `blue`.
  - [ ] Multi-line `@props`/`@aware` arrays (e.g. `@props([\n    'color' => 'blue',\n])`) parse correctly (keys bound, values excluded) — with a regression test using the multi-line format, not only the single-line one.
  - [ ] For `@props(['color' => 'blue']) <div title="literal">` on one line, the binding check returns true for `color` and false for both `blue` and `literal` — this is the concrete "unrelated quoted text" case a test must cover.
- [ ] Each of the eight fixes ships with a regression test that (a) exercises the real LSP entry point (the handler in `main.rs`, e.g. `wire_attribute_goto_definition`, `this_member_hover_card`), not only the underlying pure helper in isolation, and (b) asserts the exact value/position/classification named in that item — e.g. Item 3's test asserts goto lands on the exact `$increment = fn() => ...` line number, not merely that goto returns `Some`; Item 6's test asserts the returned line number equals the earlier class's line, not merely that `locate_member` returns a value.

Tightened the acceptance criteria after adversarial review (4 blind lenses: malicious-compliance, testability, completeness, edge-case). Real gaps closed:

- **Item 1:** the walk must index `<livewire:...>` usage as well as `<x-...>` (three lenses independently caught this — the issue names both syntaxes, the original AC's example only exercised one); cycle guard must be a visited-set, not a depth cap; sort key named explicitly (lexicographic path); added precedence, partial-cycle-pruning, and no-ancestor test cases the issue implies but didn't spell out.
- **Item 2:** fallback must not regress already-correct named-class hover cards; disk-vs-buffer disagreement (flagged in the issue itself) must be fixed or explicitly deferred, not silently dropped.
- **Item 3:** `computed()`/`action()`-wrapped Volt forms (which the codebase's own `VOLT_FUNCTIONAL_CALLS` already detects) were missing from the AC's examples; functional-Volt hover inherits Item 2's `"Component"` bug and needs its own test.
- **Item 4:** the issue's own warning — `wire:target` naming a property under `wire:model` loading state breaks once Item 5 lands — wasn't required to be handled or preserved. Now it is.
- **Item 5:** scope was goto-only; hover and completion share the same kind-agnostic primitive and need the same fix and a test.
- **Item 6:** "sort by line" can still be satisfied by BFS reordering without true document order — pinned to a `(line, column)` sort over a full traversal; scoping fix widened from "traits/enums" to "every other top-level declaration," since the leak isn't trait-specific.
- **Item 7:** "Salsa-cached" was unfalsifiable — pinned to `#[salsa::tracked]` plus an explicit invalidation test (edit the backing class, confirm the cache updates) and a call-count test, since cache correctness, not just cache existence, is the real risk here.
- **Item 8:** multi-line `@props`/`@aware` (the common Blade style) was untested; added a concrete example for "unrelated quoted text."
- **General:** tests must exercise the real LSP handler, not just the pure helper in isolation — several items had a "fix the function, never rewire the caller" loophole.

Net effect: every one of the 8 sub-items grew cross-cutting dependencies on at least one other (1↔7, 2↔3, 4↔5, 5 itself widened to touch 3 call sites). That's relevant to right-sizing below.

<!-- lestrade-oversized-unit -->
@mikebronner the coherent unit of work here — everything this issue collects — can't ship as one coherent PR: it's 8 explicitly enumerated follow-ups spanning a one-line attribute reclassification (item 4) to a Salsa-backed reverse-index graph walk with cycle detection (item 1). AC verification (4 blind lenses) made this worse, not better: it surfaced real cross-item dependencies the flat list hid — item 1 needs item 7's Salsa caching to land first (the issue says so directly: *"Item 1's graph walk should not be built on top of it until this is addressed"*), item 3's hover fix inherits item 2's bug, and item 5's Method/Property filtering has to touch goto, hover, *and* completion, which pulls item 4 along with it. That's not one deliverable, it's a dependency graph.

**Options**

1. **Re-author as 6 sub-issues under #339 as a tracking parent**, using this project's own `Parent issue`/`Sub-issues progress` fields, grouped by the dependency clusters the AC review found: (a) item 7 — Salsa caching, ships first; (b) item 1 — up-walk navigation, blocked on (a); (c) item 6 — traversal order + completion scoping, independent; (d) items 2+3 — hover-label fix + functional Volt wiring, coupled; (e) items 4+5 — `wire:target` classification + Method/Property kind-filtering across goto/hover/completion, coupled; (f) item 8 — `@props` binding fix, fully independent, smallest. I'd re-triage each with its own AC/WSJF and use `add_blocked_by` to encode (a)→(b) natively. *Pros:* each PR is independently reviewable and revertable, matches the board's existing native support for this. *Cons:* 6x the triage/review overhead instead of 1.
2. **Split into 2 issues** — "architecture/perf" (items 6+7) vs "feature fixes" (items 1,2,3,4,5,8). *Pros:* only one extra re-triage. *Cons:* doesn't actually fix the problem — the "feature fixes" bucket still bundles 6 items with the same 1↔7, 2↔3, 4↔5 cross-dependencies the tightening pass just found, so it's still not one coherent PR.
3. **Ship as one PR anyway.** *Pros:* no re-authoring overhead. *Cons:* runs straight into the pipeline's own #1 rejection category (correctness, ~102 tracked events) — an 8-way, cross-cutting, 30+-criterion PR is exactly the shape that produces multi-round bounces, and one merge/revert takes down 8 unrelated fixes together.

**Recommendation:** option 1. The dependency clusters aren't my invention — they came out of the issue's own text plus adversarial AC review — and the board already has the field to model a parent/sub-issue split. Six focused PRs will clear Holmes review faster than one that tries to be all eight at once.

issues.title: Translation completion previews the alphabetically-first locale, not the app's configured locale
issues.body:
Found while reviewing #336. Pre-existing on `main` — not introduced by that PR, which only reuses the same rule for namespaced catalogues.

## What happens

Translation-key completion always sources its values from the **alphabetically first** locale directory, not the application's configured locale.

`TranslationCache::completion_keys` (`laravel-lsp/src/salsa_impl.rs:1974`):

```rust
let mut candidates = locales_in_dir(&*db, listing).clone();
candidates.sort();
let Some(locale) = candidates.first().cloned() else {
    return Vec::new();
};
```

The code comment is candid about it:

> Alphabetical is arbitrary but stable, and matches how `locales` orders.

That sort was the right fix for the bug it addressed — `locales_in_dir` preserves directory-listing order, which is filesystem-dependent (APFS sorts, ext4 doesn't), so completion results varied by platform and CI caught it on ubuntu while macOS stayed green. Sorting made it deterministic. It just made it deterministically *wrong* for any project whose default locale isn't alphabetically first.

## Why it matters

For a project with `lang/de/`, `lang/en/`, `lang/fr/` and `'locale' => 'en'` in `config/app.php`, every completion detail shows the **German** string. The keys are right; the values previewed next to them are from a locale the app never renders by default.

Alphabetical order puts `ar`, `de`, and `cs` ahead of `en`, so this hits a large share of multilingual projects — and silently, since the keys themselves look correct.

## Suggested fix

`app.locale` is never read anywhere in the codebase today (`grep -rn "app\.locale\|fallback_locale" laravel-lsp/src` returns nothing), but the machinery to read it already exists:

1. Resolve `config_lookup::resolve_value(root, "app.locale")`.
2. Use that locale's directory when it exists among the candidates.
3. Fall back to `config_lookup::resolve_value(root, "app.fallback_locale")`.
4. Fall back to the current sorted-first behaviour when neither resolves — keeping today's determinism guarantee intact for projects where the config can't be read.

Worth noting `resolve_value` returns the raw source text, so an `env('APP_LOCALE', 'en')` expression will need unwrapping to its default argument — the same shape the existing `env()` handling already deals with elsewhere.

## Scope

The same first-locale rule now applies in two places after #336 lands — the root catalogue scan and the namespaced-catalogue scan it adds. Both should read from the same resolved locale, so this is best fixed once in `completion_keys` rather than at each call site.

## Not in scope

Hover and goto for translation keys resolve through a different path and are not affected by this. This is specifically the completion detail/value preview.
